Send button fill on iOS is a lighter/desaturated pink compared to the slightly more saturated pink in React, causing most of the 1.99% pixel mismatch.
Internal padding, alignment, and component bounds within the composer appear equivalent between the two platforms.
No missing elements; layout scaling looks consistent at the composite's relative size.
likelyCauses: iOS is rendering the disabled/pink CTA background with a platform-specific tint (e.g. system UIColor or asset color) rather than the exact token used in React.
Possible alpha or sRGB color-space difference between web and iOS color management for the pink state.
suggestedFixes: Sample the React send-button hex and match it in the iOS color asset (or SwiftUI / UIKit color definition) used for the composer's primary CTA pink.
Confirm the color token is defined once in the shared design-token source and consumed identically on both platforms.
Re-run the visual diff after the color fix; expect RGB similarity to rise above ~99%.
intentional: Differences in overall canvas size (342x100 vs 1170x2532) reflect platform capture dimensions, not a layout regression.

cases.title: Thread Composer States

summary: Crop offset: Android image is offset by 24px on the x-axis compared to React, causing horizontal shift in the entire composer block
The pink send button in Android appears slightly larger and shifted right within its frame
Text 'Review the Android composer crop' appears at slightly different vertical position due to crop offset
Attachment icon buttons (image, paperclip) are positioned at different horizontal locations between the two renders
As Task checkbox and label appear with slight horizontal offset between renders
likelyCauses: Android crop rectangle was defined with x=24 offset instead of x=0, shifting the comparison canvas
Possible manual-rect crop misconfiguration in the Android screenshot capture pipeline
Baseline uses 'element' crop mode while current uses 'manual-rect', causing alignment drift
suggestedFixes: Update the Android crop rect x value from 24 to 0 to match React baseline alignment
Switch Android crop mode from 'manual-rect' to 'element' with contract 'component-bounds' for consistent capture
Re-run the visual diff after fixing crop offset to verify remaining pixel mismatch
Verify the Slock capture pipeline for Android uses the same origin point as React for element bounds
Inspect send button sizing token in Android theme to ensure it matches React's 32×32 pink square spec

summary: Composer card bounding box is significantly wider on iOS (1170px canvas) versus React baseline, but internal layout, spacing, and component arrangement remain visually consistent.
Header text "Review the Android composer crop", icon attachments (image, paperclip), "As Task" checkbox, and pink send button are present in both with matching relative positions.
Font weight, size, and color of header/body text appear equivalent between React and iOS renders.
Attachment icon buttons and send button shapes/sizes are proportionally similar; no clipping or missing elements detected.
All interactive state indicators (checkbox square, pink filled send button) render identically in both versions.
likelyCauses: Canvas viewport difference: iOS baseline rendered into 1170×2532 canvas versus React's 342×100 component-bounds crop, causing perceived scale but not actual layout drift.
Slight rasterization/antialiasing differences between rendering engines contributing to the 2.10% pixel mismatch and 84.3% RGB similarity drop despite structural equivalence.
suggestedFixes: Verify the iOS snapshot crop contract matches React's component-bounds crop so visual diffs aren't comparing canvas vs. element regions.
If component scaling is intentional, normalize the comparison crop region on the iOS side to align 1:1 with the React 342×100 baseline.
Re-run the comparison with the correct element-bounds crop on iOS to confirm whether the remaining 2.1% mismatch is purely antialiasing noise.
Confirm font rendering tokens (weight, size, family) are shared between React and iOS implementations to prevent future text-weight drift.
Document that the pink send button and attachment icon set are platform-consistent and require no action.
intentional: Wider iOS canvas vs. compact React card is expected due to different device viewport and crop strategy.
RGB similarity 84.3% is below typical threshold but pixel-perfect 97.9% indicates structural equivalence; remaining diff is likely antialiasing.

summary: Body text 'Review the Android composer crop' renders slightly larger/bolder on iOS (right) compared to Android (left), with marginally thicker strokes.
The 'As Task' label appears visually heavier/bolder on iOS than on Android; the small square glyph before it is also slightly larger on iOS.

Left toolbar icons (gallery-plus, paperclip) appear marginally smaller and with thinner strokes on iOS; the send/paper-plane icon (pink) is the same color but the icon glyph itself is subtly smaller on iOS.
Checkbox/As Task and send button are positioned slightly higher (less vertical padding from the top text baseline) on iOS, making the toolbar row feel tighter top-to-bottom on iOS.
Right-side pink send button has a slightly more saturated/intense pink on iOS vs. a slightly softer pink on Android; icon centering inside the button differs by ~1–2px between platforms.
likelyCauses: Platform default font metrics differ (SF Pro on iOS vs. Roboto on Android) leading to subtle weight and size drift at the same DP.
Iconography source assets not being normalized to a shared baseline grid; SVG/vector stroke widths not platform-adjusted.
Color tokens for the accent pink (send button) resolve to slightly different sRGB values per platform theme.
Vertical padding/spacing tokens resolved using native safe-area/insets that differ between iOS and Android.
suggestedFixes: Normalize the composer body text to an explicit font-size/line-height token (e.g. 16/22 DP) instead of relying on platform default text styles.
Force a shared icon size and stroke width for the toolbar action icons (gallery-plus, paperclip, send) via a single token.
Align the accent color of the send button to a single design token; verify both Android and iOS themes map to the same hex.
Standardize the toolbar row vertical padding (e.g. 8 DP top/bottom) and re-check that 'As Task' and send button share the same baseline.
Re-run the visual test with a fixed-content composer (no dynamic state) to confirm divergences are stable across runs.
intentional: Different device aspect ratios (1026×300 Android vs. 1170×2532 iOS) producing different overall canvas height — expected.
Platform-native font family substitution (Roboto vs. SF Pro) at the document level — expected unless explicitly overridden.

cases.title: Thread Composer Member Suggestions

summary: In 'IN THIS CHANNEL' list, the order of the first two rows is swapped: React shows 'artin' (yellow highlight) then 'Cindy'; Android shows 'Cindy' (yellow highlight) then 'Product UX...'
The highlighted (selected) row differs between platforms: React highlights the avatar-only 'artin' entry, Android highlights the full 'Cindy' row that includes bio and @mention text

Text clipping in 'NOT IN THIS CHANNEL' section on Android: 'Android De...' and 'I work...' descriptions overlap the @Product-UX-Designer handle, producing illegible stacked/overlapping text (React shows clean truncation with ellipsis)
Section/card spacing is larger on Android: more vertical gap between 'IN THIS CHANNEL' and 'NOT IN THIS CHANNEL' cards, and between the suggestions panel and the composer toolbar
Composer toolbar layout is more compact on Android: icon group (image, attachment) sits closer to the @ glyph, and the 'As Task' checkbox/send button cluster is shifted further right than in React
likelyCauses: Suggestion list data shape or ordering differs between the React and Android member-suggestions components (likely different list item model / row layout)
Android member suggestion row item uses a single dense layout (name + description + @handle in one row) versus React's multi-row layout
Selected-state highlight is bound to a different row index due to list ordering or keyboard/focus divergence between platforms
Text truncation / ellipsizing on Android is not applied per-line, causing description and @handle to wrap on top of each other
Avatar fallback asset/color is not tokenized consistently across platforms
suggestedFixes: Unify the member-suggestion row layout across platforms: adopt a consistent two-line pattern (name on line 1, description + @handle truncated on line 2) with proper single-line ellipsization to prevent overlap
Align the list ordering so the currently-highlighted/selected item is index 0 in both React and Android implementations
Apply ellipsize=end to both the description and @handle TextViews, and cap each to a single line with adequate horizontal padding
Tokenize avatar fallback colors and shapes so both platforms render the same placeholder (e.g., purple silhouette) when an avatar image is missing
Reconcile vertical spacing tokens between the 'IN THIS CHANNEL' and 'NOT IN THIS CHANNEL' section cards and the gap to the composer toolbar

summary: Different list item ordering: React highlights 'artin' (avatar placeholder, no bot indicator) as selected, while iOS highlights 'Cindy' (bot avatar, with status dot) as selected.

iOS 'IN THIS CHANNEL' section shows secondary text (status/preview like 'Keeps visual testing releas...', 'T...') inline with name; React shows it only on the non-selected row and omits it on the selected 'artin' row.
iOS renders all 'NOT IN THIS CHANNEL' avatars with the bot/checkered pattern, while React uses a generic person placeholder for 'artin' and a solid teal block for 'Product UX De…'.
Selection highlight placement differs: iOS highlights the second visible row (Cindy) instead of the first row, and uses a wider yellow band that extends closer to the right edge including the handle.
Bottom composer toolbar on iOS is detached/floating below the suggestions card with extra vertical gap, whereas React places it directly attached beneath the suggestion list.
likelyCauses: iOS implementation reorders the suggestion list or shifts the keyboard-focus/highlighted index relative to the React baseline.
iOS renders richer secondary metadata (status message, truncated preview) on each row while the React variant shows it only on hover/non-selected state.
Avatar assets differ per platform: iOS uses the bot-style checkered avatar for all entries, React uses placeholder silhouettes or solid color blocks.
Spacing/padding tokens (row height, inner padding, toolbar separation) were not normalized across the two platform implementations.
suggestedFixes: Verify selected/highlighted row index matches the React baseline (first entry, 'artin') and align list ordering logic if iOS re-sorts.
Match secondary text rendering per row so the preview/status string appears consistently on both selected and non-selected items.
Align avatar rendering so placeholder vs bot avatars are consistent across platforms (or accept as platform-specific asset if intentional).
Normalize list row height and internal padding to the React spec; reduce vertical gap between the suggestions card and the composer toolbar.
Confirm whether iOS composer attachment below the card is intentional platform behavior or should be moved flush against the suggestions card.
intentional: Platform-specific avatar assets for bot vs person indicators may be acceptable as native conventions.
Detached floating composer on iOS may be an intentional iOS keyboard-avoidance pattern.

cases.title: Thread Files List

summary: Typography: Android renders filenames and metadata in a lighter weight than React (React is bold/semi-bold).
Date format differs: React shows 'Jun 25, 10:24 AM' while Android shows 'Jun 25, 10:24' (AM suffix missing).
State indicator divergence: Android shows an extra 'Downloading 44%' status row under release-notes.pdf; React shows no progress state.
Download icon swap: Android replaces the download-arrow button on release-notes.pdf with a cancel/stop (C) icon — different component/asset.
Component bounds / row height: Android rows are vertically taller, pushing the 'Load more' button lower and right-shifted relative to React.
likelyCauses: Android typography stack not mapping to the same font weight/size tokens as React (system Roboto/Compose default vs web font).
Locale/time formatter on Android omits AM/PM (24-hour locale or missing 'a' pattern token).
Download progress UI is being rendered conditionally on Android but suppressed (or mocked) in React baseline, producing different row states.
Action icon set divergence: Android renders a cancel glyph for in-progress downloads while React baselines the download glyph only.
Vertical padding/density tokens differ between platforms, inflating row and overall list height.
suggestedFixes: Align Android text styles for file name (titleMedium/bold) and metadata (bodySmall/regular) to match React tokens.
Use a time formatter that includes the AM/PM suffix (e.g., 'MMM dd, hh:mm a') on Android to mirror React.
Ensure the 'Downloading %' progress row is either shown or hidden consistently across both platforms, and gate it behind the same condition.
Map the in-progress download action to the cancel icon in both platforms, or render the download icon only on idle state in both.
Reconcile row vertical padding/density tokens so list item heights match the React baseline.
intentional: Possibly intentional use of system fonts on Android yielding different perceived weight.
Potential intentional platform-specific download-state action (cancel vs download).

Normalize placeholder behavior so both ends show the same fallback graphic when the thumbnail asset is unavailable
Confirm the iOS Image component is not suppressing the placeholder during/after load

cases.title: Thread Header States

summary: Header subtitle on Android truncates earlier ('Home she...') compared to React baseline ('Home shell,' appears partially visible but more aggressive truncation vs React).
Android badge counter shows '4' next to the members icon, while React baseline shows '0'.
Android header is missing the search (magnifier), notifications (bell), and unread message (square) icon buttons present in React between the title and settings gear icon.
Settings gear icon and members avatar icon are positioned far to the right on Android, nearly clipped against the right edge, whereas they sit closer to the other header actions in React.

Tab bar in React has 3 tabs (Chat, Tasks, Files) where the third tab uses the full remaining width; Android renders only 2 tabs (Chat, Tasks, Files label only) with the Files tab taking remaining width and no visible third empty tab cell.
likelyCauses: Android implementation is omitting the search, notifications, and unread-channel icon buttons from the header toolbar.
Badge value differs due to stale or test data divergence between platforms (React shows 0, Android shows 4).
Subtitle text container on Android has a narrower max-width / smaller truncation region than the React baseline.
Header action group uses justify-content/flex-end on Android with insufficient padding, pushing the rightmost icons to the canvas edge.
suggestedFixes: Add the missing search, notification bell, and unread-square icon buttons to the Android ThreadHeader to match React's icon order and spacing.
Ensure the notification badge reflects the same unread count as React (or align both to a shared state source).
Increase the subtitle TextView maxWidth / set the same ellipsize margins so the truncated preview matches React baseline length.
Add right padding (e.g., 12–16dp) to the header action row so gear and members icons don't hug the screen edge.
Re-check tab bar implementation so the Files tab styling and width distribution mirror the React baseline.
intentional: Differences in icon library rendering between React and Android may be expected if cross-platform icon parity is not a requirement.

summary: Username 'Cindy' is significantly larger and bolder on Android than on React (React title and metadata text sizes appear swapped/scaled).
Preview line wraps to two lines on Android but fits on one line on React due to larger text size.
Metadata line ('Keeps vis…' and timestamp) is clipped/truncated on React ('Keeps vis…', '02:30 AM') but fully shown on Android ('Keeps visual testing …', '10:30').

likelyCauses: Android typography scale (sp/font-size) for thread row title/body is larger than React's token mapping.
Android uses a different text-truncation policy (no ellipsis) and larger line-height, causing wrap and pushing controls out of bounds.
Reaction/reply count chip component not rendered or measured with insufficient height on Android.

Set Android maxLines + ellipsize on preview/metadata so layout height stays at 108dp and prevents wrapping.

Remove the light-blue background on #product:… mention token on Android, or add it to React for parity.
Normalize timestamp formatting to a single locale/format across platforms.
intentional: Avatar rendering and presence dot appear consistent across both sides.
Overall container bounds (374×108) are identical.
RGB similarity 85.2% with mostly text-scaling-driven pixel mismatch suggests layout drift rather than missing components.

declaredDivergences.description: Chip fill/border paint past the glyphs without reserving the box width in layout, so the border-to-neighbor gap approximates React's inline-block advance (atomic box rewrite tracked as task #448).
Long inline code wraps via the shared zero-width-space bridge (slockInlineCodeCharWrapBridgeThreshold), not native char-level wrap (task #401 A-bridge).

Add a visual-regression check on the comment-anchor thread component asserting border thickness parity between Android and iOS snapshots.
Audit other components in the thread (buttons, inputs, cards) for the same border-weight delta and normalize in one pass.

likelyCauses: Independent scaling between web and iOS responsive layouts (no shared design token enforcement).

Different font scale and line-height defaults between web (browser) and iOS (system font).

summary: Typography: iOS renders all text (labels, headings, inputs, buttons, link text) with a noticeably heavier/bolder weight than Android, particularly visible in 'Sign In', 'Email', 'Password', button labels, and the 'Terms of Service' / 'Privacy Policy' / 'Create One' link row.

likelyCauses: Kuikly text style not normalizing font-weight / font-family across Android and iOS (system font SF Pro on iOS vs Roboto on Android producing different perceived weight at the same dp).
Container padding/margin tokens not shared across platforms (dp-to-pt conversion or per-platform style overrides).
Button and input component styles specifying fixed pixel heights instead of density-independent values, causing different heights at the 390×844 vs 1170×2532 canvas.
Platform-specific stroke/border thickness defaults being applied differently on iOS.
Missing baseline alignment contract so no single source of truth for spacing tokens.
suggestedFixes: Define font-weight explicitly (e.g., 400/500/600) in the shared style sheet so SF Pro and Roboto map to visually equivalent weights.
Convert all input/button heights and paddings to density-independent units and apply a shared spacing token (e.g., 8/12/16/24 dp) verified on both ends.
Audit border/stroke widths on TextField and Button components; unify to a single tokenized border width.
Normalize the header banner height with a fixed dp value or percentage token rather than letting it scale with raw pixels.
Run a side-by-side diff at identical dp (not raw px) so future regressions surface as ratio, not pixel mismatch.
